His five-pointed otherness (suggested through pentagram geometry) doesn't fit the four-square mesh of the city's nets, so the nets bunch, tangle, bind harder. Others pass through the city's nets with some freedom but he's caught at every step. The palette emphasizes the excess - muddy greens and browns layered thick, the hung-over crushing multiplied. The outsider doesn't escape nets but gets extra ones.

nets-5.name: Identity of Nets
nets-5.description: Finding others by recognizing their nets - the karass of the entangled. Forging identity through shared crushing triviality. Understanding what you are through recognizing their guilt, their resentments, their petty obligations. We are those who are caught.

meaning.upright: Recognizing others by seeing their nets. Identity forged through shared entanglement: we are the guilty, the obligated, the hung-over, the crushed by triviality. Finding your people through their resentments matching yours. The karass revealed as those caught in similar nets. What you are: one who knows these particular petty crushing things.
meaning.inverted: Identity as only your nets - 'I am my entanglements and nothing else.' Finding others to share misery, making it identity. Recognition becoming competition over who's more entangled. The karass as cult of resentment. Forging identity through nets you won't release because then who would you be?

instructions.style_guidance: Two figures recognizing each other through visible nets. Connection through shared entanglement. Tangled lines connecting them - not flowing circles but irregular binding threads.
instructions.content_guidance: Two entangled figures recognizing each other. Their nets touch or connect. The moment of 'you're caught too' recognition. Identity through shared crushing triviality.
instructions.detailed_description: Two figures (Stephen and perhaps another outsider) stand across tangled Dublin space, both wrapped in nets. Their nets reach toward each other, touch, connect - recognition through shared entanglement. One's guilt-net touches the other's obligation-net. Nationality binds one, language the other, but both are caught and both see it. The moment of 'oh, there you are' but dark: you're entangled like I'm entangled, therefore we're kin. Not beautiful recognition but recognition nonetheless. The karass of the caught. Identity forged in the smithy of resentment and petty crushing things. Irregular tangled lines connect them, not mandala but mesh. Muddy palette, compressed space.

nets-6.name: Asymmetry of Nets
nets-6.description: Seven nets when balance requires six or eight. The crushing realization that your entanglements are uneven, asymmetric, won't resolve into anything clean. Some obligations heavier than others, some resentments deeper, and no way to balance it. The odd net out that makes everything worse.

meaning.upright: Understanding your nets don't balance, can't be made even. Seven obligations that won't pair or cancel. The asymmetry of entanglement: some nets heavier, some tighter, no clean resolution. Recognizing the uneven crushing weight without falling into self-pity. You're entangled asymmetrically and that's truth.
meaning.inverted: Asymmetry as justification - 'I'm more entangled than anyone, so I can do anything.' The uneven nets as permanent grievance. Using asymmetric obligations to avoid all obligation. The odd position cultivated: 'My nets are special, no one understands.' Asymmetry as excuse for cruelty or inaction.

instructions.style_guidance: Seven nets arranged to show uncomfortable asymmetry. Uneven tangling, some nets heavier/tighter than others. The imbalance visible and oppressive. No clean lines, no resolution.
instructions.content_guidance: Seven nets in asymmetric arrangement - three tight on one side, four loose on the other, but neither side better. Figure caught in the imbalance. The uneven crushing visible.
instructions.detailed_description: Seven nets bind a figure (Stephen) in asymmetric arrangement. Three nets on one side are tight, cutting: guilt over his mother, obligation to the tower, debt to Mulligan. Four nets on the other side are looser but more numerous: teaching job, students' indifference, Deasy's antisemitism, the whole crushing morning. They don't balance. Three plus four equals seven and seven can't be made even. The figure's posture shows the asymmetry - pulled harder one way but more entangled the other. No way to balance these obligations. The irregular tangled mesh emphasizes: this won't resolve. Muddy palette, compressed space showing the uncomfortable uneven crushing.

nets-7.name: History of Nets
nets-7.description: All the nets ever cast, accumulating through time. History is a nightmare from which I am trying to awake - and history is nets layered on nets on nets. Every generation's petty obligations added to the crushing weight. The ocean that drowns rather than carries.

meaning.upright: Understanding nets accumulate through history. All the petty obligations, resentments, guilts of those who came before become yours. History as nightmare of entanglement: each generation added nets, none removed them. The crushing weight of inherited triviality. Pattern revealing itself: they were caught, you're caught, everyone will be caught. What brought you here: all who were entangled before you.
meaning.inverted: History as excuse - 'I'm entangled because of the past, so I can't act now.' The nightmare embraced, wallowed in. Using accumulated nets as reason to never try escape. The ocean of entanglement as identity. Pattern as predetermination - 'they were caught so I must be.' History as justification for remaining netted.

instructions.style_guidance: Layers of nets visible simultaneously through time. Ancient to modern, all tangled together. Overwhelming accumulation. The weight visible, crushing. No ocean-as-support here, only drowning.
instructions.content_guidance: Nets layered through time - old nets at bottom, recent nets on top, all tangling together. Figure drowning in accumulated entanglement. History as crushing weight of nets.
instructions.detailed_description: The composition shows nets through time, layered like sediment or nightmare. Ancient nets at bottom - Celtic obligations, tribal debts. Medieval nets middle - church obligations, feudal duties. Colonial nets - British rule, poverty, emigration. Modern nets top - teaching job, tower rent, student indifference. All tangling together into one massive crushing mesh. A young figure (Stephen) struggles in this accumulated weight, not swimming but drowning. The nets press down with weight of centuries. History isn't ocean that might carry you home but ocean of nets that drowns. Every generation added to the weight. The nightmare visible and inescapable. Muddy greens and browns layered thick, compressed space showing centuries of crushing triviality accumulated.

nets-8.name: Invitation of Nets
nets-8.description: The moment before choosing to enter more nets willingly. Invitation to new obligations, new entanglements, offered as opportunity. The breath before saying yes to what will crush you. The threshold where you could refuse the nets but probably won't.

meaning.upright: Standing before new nets being offered. Understanding they're nets but considering entry anyway. The invitation might be genuine - new job, new relationship, new obligation - but nets nonetheless. Threshold moment where you see the entanglement clearly before choosing it. The breath before accepting new crushing triviality. What's offered: more of what has always caught you.
meaning.inverted: Invitation as trap recognized but entered anyway. The threshold crossed despite knowing it's nets. Self-destructive acceptance of new entanglements. The breath before deliberate self-ensnarement. What's offered and accepted: the crushing weight you claim you don't want but keep choosing.

instructions.style_guidance: A doorway or threshold hung with nets. Someone standing before it, seeing the nets clearly, moment of choice visible. Not yet caught but about to be. Compressed, tangled, the invitation visible as nets.
instructions.content_guidance: New nets hanging in doorway - a job offer, a relationship, a new obligation visibly made of nets. Figure at threshold, hand reaching toward the nets but not yet caught. The moment before choosing.
instructions.detailed_description: A threshold, door standing open, but the doorway is hung with nets - visible, obvious, undeniable nets. A figure (Stephen or any young person) stands before it, hand reaching out, seeing the nets clearly. This might be a new teaching job, a romantic possibility, a familial obligation - but it's shown as nets. The figure's face shows they know it's nets but are considering entering anyway. Behind them, escape (?) but also isolation. Through the netted doorway, something that might be good but will definitely entangle. The moment of invitation held in suspension: you can see what this is, will you enter? The breath before probably saying yes to new crushing triviality. Muddy palette, compressed space, the nets undeniable.

nets-9.name: Recurrence of Nets
nets-9.description: The crushing understanding: nets will catch you again and again. Escaping one net means entering another. Finishing one set of petty obligations reveals another waiting. The Viconian cycle of entanglement - you're caught, you escape (sort of), you're caught again. The eternal return of being tangled.

meaning.upright: Understanding the cycle: escape one net, enter another, escape that, enter another. Recurrence as pattern recognized - nets are eternal, you will always be caught. Finishing one entanglement reveals the next waiting. Not wisdom but recognition of nightmare's structure. The cycle of petty obligations that never ends. Accepting that trying to be net-free is itself a net.
meaning.inverted: Condemned to nets forever, that's your excuse for everything. The cycle as justification for never trying escape. Recurrence embraced: 'I'll always be caught so why struggle?' Using eternal return as reason to make nets tighter. The wheel of entanglement you spin yourself, calling it fate.

instructions.style_guidance: Circular composition showing nets repeating. Spiral or ouroboros of entanglement. End becoming beginning through tangled mesh. The cycle oppressive and clear.
instructions.content_guidance: Nets arranged in circle or spiral. Last net opening into first net again. Or one net whose escaping becomes entering. The cycle of entanglement made visible.
instructions.detailed_description: Ten nets arrange themselves in a circle or spiral of nightmare. Each net represents an entanglement: leaving tower enters teaching net, leaving teaching enters debt net, leaving debt enters guilt net, and so on. The final net - attempted escape from all nets - reveals itself as the first net again: the tower, the obligations, the crushing triviality. The cycle is explicit, eternal. Or alternatively: a single net shown in spiral repetition, escaping one side means entering the other side, the ouroboros of entanglement. A figure moves through this cycle, understanding dawning: this is the pattern. Not individual failures but the structure of nets. You're caught, you'll escape, you'll be caught again. Viconian recirculation of petty crushing obligations. Muddy palette throughout, compressed space, the wheel that crushes rather than carries.

nets-10.name: Child of Nets
nets-10.description: Young Stephen wrapped in nets from birth. The child learning that everything entangles, everything crushes, everything obligates. Youth experiencing the nets for the first time as crushing - before you learn they're just always there. The child caught in triviality.

meaning.upright: Youth experiencing nets as fresh wounds. The Child of Nets feels every obligation as new crushing weight. Learning for first time that family, faith, nation all entangle. Unformed but already caught. Brilliance and sensitivity making nets hurt more. The child who doesn't yet know nets are permanent, still thinks escape is possible through youth and genius.
meaning.inverted: Youth arrested in net-resentment forever. The eternal child who uses being caught as excuse for all behavior. Unformed not from youth but from refusal to grow past entanglement. Brilliance wasted in cataloging petty obligations. The child who will never be anything but caught because that's identity now.

instructions.style_guidance: Young figure wrapped in nets that seem fresh, new-catching. The hurt of first entanglement visible. Still tangled and claustrophobic but with youth's shock at being caught.
instructions.content_guidance: Young Stephen or any child wrapped in nets - family obligations, religious guilt, national demands. The nets newer, tighter, hurting more because unexpected. The child caught.
instructions.detailed_description: A young thin figure (teenage Stephen) wrapped in nets that are fresh, still tightening, the wounds new. Family nets bind his arms: mother's expectations, father's disappointments, siblings' needs. Religious nets wrap his torso: confession's obligations, mass attendance, theological questions that trap. National nets tangle his legs: Ireland's demands, language's limitations, history's weight. He struggles not because the nets are tighter than adults' nets but because he doesn't yet know they're permanent. His face shows shock, pain, the fresh hurt of discovering everything entangles. Books nearby show his attempt to think his way out. The Child of Nets who believes, still, that genius might mean escape. Muddy palette, compressed space, the nets seeming to tighten as you watch.

nets-11.name: Father of Nets
nets-11.description: Simon Dedalus or any father wrapped in nets so long they're invisible to him now. The Father of Nets has been caught so long he doesn't see the nets, just calls it life. Could teach the child about entanglement but is too entangled to recognize it. Nets as permanent condition accepted without question.

meaning.upright: Understanding nets so long you don't see them anymore. The Father of Nets is wrapped but calls it normal, obligated but calls it duty, caught but calls it life. Could offer wisdom about entanglement but has none - been netted too long to notice. Not malicious but unable to teach because unable to see what's obvious to the child. The father who would help but is too caught himself.
meaning.inverted: Father actively casting nets at the child. Entanglement as tradition to be passed down. Teaching the wrong lessons: 'the nets are good, accept them, stop struggling.' The father who uses his own caught state to demand child be caught too. Misery demanding company through generations.

instructions.style_guidance: Middle-aged figure so thoroughly netted it's almost invisible - the nets have become him. Compressed, tangled, but not struggling. The father with nets (but unseeing).
instructions.content_guidance: Middle-aged man (Simon Dedalus or archetypal father) wrapped in nets but unaware. The nets faded into him, become his skin. Maybe offering advice to young figure, unable to see he's netted himself. The father caught.
instructions.detailed_description: A middle-aged man stands wrapped in layer upon layer of nets, but the nets have faded into grey-brown, become almost his skin, invisible to him. Work obligations, family duties, social expectations, debts, resentments - all tangled around him but he no longer struggles because he no longer sees them. He might be reaching toward the Child of Nets, offering advice, unable to recognize he's speaking from within his own entanglement. Behind him, evidence of decades of being caught: unpaid bills as nets, disappointed wife as nets, dead dreams as nets. But his face shows he thinks this is just life, normal, everyone is like this. The Father of Nets who could warn but doesn't know there's anything to warn about. Muddy palette, everything compressed, the nets so thoroughly entangling they're invisible.

nets-12.name: Mother of Nets
nets-12.description: May Dedalus dying, the ultimate net cast at Stephen. The mother's nets are guilt and love tangled together, impossible to refuse, impossible to accept. She holds the ground that the nets are staked in. The mother whose love is a net that won't release even in death.

meaning.upright: Understanding mother-love as the deepest net. She doesn't cast nets maliciously but her love, her needs, her dying all entangle completely. The guilt that won't release even after death. Ground that nets are staked in: maternal obligation, filial duty, love as crushing weight. She is the center of family nets, not creating them but being them. The mother whose requests are commands, whose love is prison.
meaning.inverted: Mother as deliberate ensnarer, using love as weapon. Nets cast with full knowledge they'll crush. Guilt wielded consciously. The mother who devours through obligation, who ensures you can never escape because escape would be betrayal. Love perverted entirely into entrapment.

instructions.style_guidance: Female figure (dying or dead) at center of net-web. All nets radiate from her. Not malicious but inescapable. Tangled, claustrophobic, the mother as center of entanglement.
instructions.content_guidance: May Dedalus or archetypal mother in bed, dying or as ghost. Nets radiate from her - family obligations, guilt, love all tangled. Stephen caught in these nets. The mother with nets (but as their center).
instructions.detailed_description: A woman (May Dedalus) lies in bed, dying or appears as ghost, and all the nets radiate from her like a spider's web. But she's not the spider - she's the center that the web is built around. Family obligation nets, guilt nets, love nets, all emanate from her suffering body. Stephen stands caught in these nets, his mother's face accusing or pleading (the 'agenbite of inwit' made visual). Her requests haunt: pray at my bedside. Her needs entangle: take care of the family. Her love is the deepest net of all because refusing it means monstrosity. Unlike the father who doesn't see his nets, she might see them but is powerless - her dying itself is a net cast at him. Everything tangled around her, everything radiating from her. The Mother of Nets who holds the ground all nets stake into. Muddy palette, compressed, claustrophobic, the guilt visible and crushing.

nets-13.name: Affirmation of Nets
nets-13.description: Can you say yes to nets? Can you affirm the crushing triviality, the petty obligations, the guilt and resentment and hangover of existence? Affirmation of Nets is the hardest yes - saying yes even to being caught, to the mundane resistance that never ends, to the nets flung at the soul.

meaning.upright: The almost-impossible affirmation: yes even to this. Yes to being caught, yes to obligations that crush, yes to petty resentments and guilt. Not celebrating nets but accepting them as part of the pattern. Yes to the struggle against nets knowing you'll be caught anyway. The hardest yes: affirming even what entraps you. Not 'I like being netted' but 'yes, this too is real, this too is life.'
meaning.inverted: Yes as Stockholm syndrome - learning to love your nets. Affirmation that's really giving up. Yes to nets as surrender to entrapment. The word emptied of meaning, yes repeated in despair not acceptance. Saying yes to what shouldn't be affirmed. Celebrating crushing triviality because that's all you know.

instructions.style_guidance: The word YES but tangled, made of nets, barely visible through the mesh. All the suit's claustrophobic tangled aesthetic trying to form affirmation. Muddy palette but the yes trying to be visible.
instructions.content_guidance: The word YES prominent but made of nets, tangled, compressed. Or nets that arrange themselves to spell yes despite their nature. Everything tangled but affirmed. The affirmation visible through crushing.
instructions.detailed_description: The word YES struggles to form in the composition, but it's made of nets - the letters themselves are tangled mesh, or nets arrange themselves to spell YES despite their nature of entanglement. The muddy green-brown palette dominates but the YES tries to glow through it. Behind or through the YES: all the previous nets - family, faith, nation, guilt, obligation, the whole crushing triviality. A figure (synthesis of Child, Father, Mother) stands within or before this tangled YES. The affirmation is visible but barely: can you say yes even to being caught? The hardest affirmation in the deck. Not celebrating nets but accepting that they're real, part of the pattern, something that gets a yes too even though it crushes. The tangled claustrophobic aesthetic of the entire suit forming, against its own nature, into affirmation. Yes even to this.

kidneys-0.name: Homecoming of Kidneys
kidneys-0.description: Bloom's actual homecoming to 7 Eccles Street. Making cocoa, climbing into bed beside Molly. The body arriving at its place of rest. Homecoming not as grand event but as ordinary comfort - familiar smells, known textures, the warmth of home as physical fact. The kidney breakfast was morning's homecoming, this is night's.

meaning.upright: Homecoming as bodily comfort. Arriving where your body can rest, be fed, be warm. The place that receives you not through grand recognition but through ordinary welcome - the bed that fits your shape, the kitchen that knows your habits. Physical arrival at physical home. The body's yes to being where it belongs. Nourishment and rest as forms of homecoming.
meaning.inverted: Homecoming without comfort - the body in the familiar place but unable to rest. Arrival at a home that no longer nourishes. The bed that fits but brings no sleep. Physical place without physical welcome. Going through homecoming's motions while the body remains uncomfortable, unfed, cold.

instructions.style_guidance: Warm, organic, rounded. The body's relief visible. Soft fabrics, domestic comfort, kitchen and bedroom warmth. Butter yellows, soft pinks, browns, the palette of nourishment and rest.
instructions.content_guidance: Bloom arriving home - making cocoa in kitchen, climbing into bed. The body at rest, being fed, being warm. Domestic comfort as arrival. The threshold of home welcoming the body.
instructions.detailed_description: The warm interior of 7 Eccles Street. In the kitchen, Bloom makes cocoa - the ritual of nourishment visible, steam rising, the kidney-bean shape prominent as the suit symbol. Soft light from a lamp. Through a doorway, the bedroom visible: Molly substantial in bed, the covers rumpled and welcoming, space for his body beside hers. Everything organic and rounded - curved furniture, soft fabrics, flesh tones. The body arriving home not to grand recognition but to comfort: a warm drink, a warm bed, familiar smells. The alpha-omega point made physical: you arrive because your body recognizes this place. Homecoming as the body's relief. Butter yellows and warm browns throughout.

kidneys-1.name: Replacement of Kidneys
kidneys-1.description: One bodily comfort succeeds another through the day. Morning's kidney breakfast gives way to lunch's sandwich. Bath replaces walking. Rest succeeds activity. The body's succession of needs met in sequence. Not rejection but rhythmic replacement - this comfort for that comfort, this nourishment for that nourishment.

meaning.upright: Understanding the body's rhythms of need and satisfaction. One comfort naturally succeeds another - eating, resting, moving, eating again. Replacement as the body's cycle: activity replaces rest which replaces activity. Not choosing between comforts but letting each have its time. The wisdom of bodily succession: breakfast gives way to lunch gives way to dinner because that's how bodies work.
meaning.inverted: Replacing one comfort with another compulsively, never satisfied. The succession of needs becoming frantic - eating but still hungry, resting but still tired. Rhythmic replacement becoming addiction to replacement itself. Unable to let any comfort last, always needing the next. Body's natural succession perverted into restless consumption.

instructions.style_guidance: Two bodily comforts in gentle transition. Morning warmth giving way to afternoon warmth. Organic curves flowing from one to another. The body's rhythm visible.
instructions.content_guidance: Two scenes of bodily comfort - kitchen breakfast becoming pub lunch, or bath becoming bed. Bloom's body moving between comforts. The gentle succession of physical satisfaction.
instructions.detailed_description: Split composition showing bodily succession: left side shows morning's comfort - the kidney sizzling, coffee brewing, Bloom's satisfaction in preparing breakfast. Right side shows afternoon's different comfort - a sandwich and burgundy at Davy Byrne's, the satisfaction of lunch, different but equally nourishing. Bloom's body is present in both, his contentment visible but different in each. The transition between them isn't rejection but flow - breakfast ends naturally, lunch begins naturally. The organic curves connect both sides - butter yellow of morning flowing into brown-red of afternoon wine. The body's wisdom: this comfort for now, that comfort for later, succession without anxiety.

kidneys-2.name: Trinity of Kidneys
kidneys-2.description: Three forms of bodily wisdom working together: nourishment, rest, and pleasure. Bloom's trinity of mundane acceptance. Food that feeds, sleep that restores, touch that delights. The three-in-one of the body living well in the everyday. Morning, afternoon, night as three forms of physical satisfaction.

meaning.upright: Understanding the body needs three kinds of care: feeding, resting, pleasuring. Trinity of bodily wisdom that together creates thriving. Nourishment without rest exhausts. Rest without pleasure dulls. Pleasure without nourishment depletes. The three supporting each other: eat well, sleep well, feel well. Morning's vigor, afternoon's contentment, night's pleasure as three aspects of one good day.
meaning.inverted: Trinity fractured - feeding without pleasure, pleasure without rest, rest without nourishment. The three at war: eating but not tasting, sleeping but not dreaming, touching but not feeling. Body's needs divided, each denying the others. The attempted satisfaction that never satisfies because parts won't work together.

instructions.style_guidance: Three bodily comforts arranged in harmonious relation. Warm colors in three registers - yellows of morning food, browns of afternoon rest, pinks of night pleasure. Organic curves connecting all three.
instructions.content_guidance: Three scenes of Bloom's bodily day: breakfast (nourishment), afternoon rest or bath (restoration), evening with Molly (pleasure). The trinity of physical care. All three necessary, all three present.
instructions.detailed_description: Three vignettes form a triangular composition. Top: morning kitchen, kidney and breakfast, nourishment - butter yellows, the feeding. Lower left: afternoon bath or rest, the body horizontal, restoration - warm browns, the resting. Lower right: evening bed with Molly, touch, pleasure - soft pinks and flesh tones, the delighting. Bloom's body present in all three, satisfied differently in each. Organic curves connect the three: the steam from cooking connects to bath steam connects to breath in bed. The trinity of bodily care that creates a good day: fed, rested, pleasured. Morning-afternoon-night. The three-in-one of living well in the body.

kidneys-3.name: The City of Kidneys
kidneys-3.description: Dublin as system of bodily comforts. Every pub offers nourishment, every corner has a place to rest, the whole city organized around the body's needs. The bounded space as place of physical satisfaction. The four-square city as four meals, four rests, four pleasures. The map of where your body can be cared for.

meaning.upright: Understanding the city as support for bodily life. Every street leads to feeding, resting, pleasuring. The bounded space offers what the body needs. Dublin knows how to care for bodies - pubs for drinking, shops for buying, beds for resting. The city as friend to physical existence. Foundation that nourishes rather than constrains. Geography as network of bodily care.
meaning.inverted: The city as desert for the body - no nourishment anywhere, no rest possible. Every street hostile to physical needs. The bounded space as starvation, exhaustion, deprivation. Foundation that denies the body what it needs. Geography as map of where you cannot be fed, cannot rest, cannot find pleasure.

instructions.style_guidance: Dublin from above, warm and welcoming. Streets as arteries bringing nourishment. Buildings as organs of care - pubs, shops, homes. Warm browns and butter yellows showing the city's capacity to feed and comfort.
instructions.content_guidance: Dublin cityscape organized around bodily comfort. Pubs prominent, butcher shops, bakeries, baths, beds. Bloom's circular route as path through nourishment. The city as body-caring organism.
instructions.detailed_description: Dublin spreads in organic curves rather than rigid grid. The Liffey flows through like an artery. The city's structures revealed as organs of bodily care: Dlugacz's butcher shop (nourishment), Davy Byrne's pub (refreshment), the Turkish bath (restoration), number 7 Eccles Street (rest and pleasure). Bloom walks his circular route, his body being cared for at each point - bought kidney here, ate lunch there, considered bath at that corner, home at journey's end. The city isn't hostile or indifferent but organized around bodies needing care. Four-square foundation but soft, supportive. Kidney-bean shapes integrated into the architecture - the suit symbol showing the city knows what bodies need. Warm palette throughout.

kidneys-4.name: The Outsider of Kidneys
kidneys-4.description: Bloom's body is different - marked as outsider but still needing feeding, rest, pleasure. His outsider position doesn't change his body's needs. Finding bodily comfort despite being marked as other. The five-pointed body that still needs to eat, sleep, feel. Physical existence transcending social exclusion.

meaning.upright: Understanding that outsider status doesn't change the body's needs. Your different body still needs feeding, resting, pleasuring. Finding comfort despite exclusion - the kidney breakfast is good regardless of who scorns you. Physical existence as democratic: all bodies need care. The outsider's body still gets hungry, tired, desirous. Bodily wisdom transcending social position.
meaning.inverted: Outsider body denied basic care. Being marked as other means denied nourishment, rest, pleasure. The different body starved, exhausted, deprived. Social exclusion becoming physical deprivation. Unable to find comfort because marked as outsider. Body's needs used to punish difference.

instructions.style_guidance: Bloom's body distinct but still needing care. Five-pointed difference visible but body still organic, still curved, still warm. The outsider who eats, rests, pleasures despite being marked.
instructions.content_guidance: Bloom eating, resting, or in bodily comfort - but his difference visible. Others might scorn but he still feeds his body. The outsider's body being cared for despite exclusion.
instructions.detailed_description: Bloom at breakfast, the kidney prominent, his body being nourished. But visible markers of otherness: perhaps a Star of David subtly present, or others in the background marking him as different. Yet his body is fed regardless - the kidney nourishes Jewish body and Irish body identically. His outsider position (five-pointed star geometry somewhere in composition) doesn't change that his body needs breakfast, needs the bath he anticipates, needs Molly's warmth. The body as great leveler: all bodies need care. Bloom's wisdom: feed your body despite their scorn. Warm palette emphasizing that nourishment works regardless of social position. The outsider whose body is still a body.

kidneys-5.name: Identity of Kidneys
kidneys-5.description: Finding others through recognizing their bodily care. The karass of those who feed themselves, rest their bodies, take pleasure in physical existence. Identity forged through shared embodied wisdom. We are those who know the body matters, who care for flesh, who find joy in the ordinary physical.

meaning.upright: Recognizing others by how they care for their bodies. Identity through shared bodily wisdom: we feed ourselves well, rest properly, take physical pleasure. Finding your people through their embodied care - they eat with attention, sleep without guilt, touch with joy. The karass revealed through mundane acceptance. What you are: one who knows bodies need tending and does the tending.
meaning.inverted: Identity only as bodily - 'I am my appetites and nothing else.' Finding others to enable excess rather than care. Recognition becoming competition over who eats more, rests more, pleasures more. The karass as cult of indulgence. Forging identity through body without consciousness, flesh without wisdom.

instructions.style_guidance: Two figures sharing bodily comfort - eating together, resting together. Warm organic connection through physical care. Curves connecting them through shared nourishment or rest.
instructions.content_guidance: Bloom and perhaps another (Molly? a companion?) sharing food or rest. Recognition through shared bodily wisdom - they both know how to care for flesh. Identity through embodied acceptance.
instructions.detailed_description: Bloom and another figure (perhaps Molly, perhaps Stephen, perhaps any embodied soul) share a meal or rest together. Their recognition isn't intellectual but physical: they both know how to feed the body, how to let it rest, how to take pleasure. Warm food between them, or warm bed holding both, showing the karass of embodied care. Their faces show the recognition: 'oh, you understand that bodies matter too.' Not reducing to only flesh but including flesh fully. Organic curves connect them - steam from shared food, warmth of shared rest, the acknowledgment of shared physical existence. Identity forged in the smithy not of soul alone but of soul-in-body. Finding the others who eat the kidney, who make the cocoa, who climb into bed knowing rest is sacred too.

kidneys-6.name: Asymmetry of Kidneys
kidneys-6.description: Seven bodily needs when balance requires six or eight. Sometimes hungrier, sometimes more tired, sometimes needier of touch. The body's asymmetric demands - some days need more feeding, some more rest. Understanding that physical care can't be perfectly balanced, rationed, scheduled. The odd bodily need out.

meaning.upright: Understanding the body's needs aren't symmetrical. Seven hungers that won't pair evenly. Some days need more food, some more sleep, some more touch - and that's the body's wisdom, not failure. Accepting asymmetric care without guilt. Feed when hungry even if 'not meal time.' Rest when tired even if 'too early.' The body knows what it needs when it needs it, and seven is fine.
meaning.inverted: Asymmetry as chaos - the body's needs out of control. Seven demands that tyrannize. Unable to manage uneven physical needs. Feeding, resting, pleasuring without pattern becoming excuse for excess. Asymmetry weaponized: 'my body needs it' justifying anything. The odd need as bottomless pit.

instructions.style_guidance: Seven bodily comforts in asymmetric but organic arrangement. Uneven but natural - more food here, less rest there, but the body satisfied. Warm palette showing health despite imbalance.
instructions.content_guidance: Seven instances of bodily care arranged asymmetrically - three meals of different sizes, four rests of different lengths, but Bloom's body well cared for despite unevenness. The asymmetry as natural.
instructions.detailed_description: Seven kidney-bean shapes arrange themselves in organic asymmetry around Bloom's body through a day. Three are large (substantial meals), four are smaller (snacks, light refreshments) - they don't balance but they nourish. Or seven rests of different lengths - some deep sleep, some brief sitting, some quick pauses. The asymmetry is visible but not problematic: the body knows what it needs when. Bloom's face shows contentment despite the uneven distribution - he ate when hungry even if not 'meal time,' rested when tired even if not 'bed time.' The seven that can't be made six or eight but feed the body fine. Warm palette throughout showing that asymmetric care works if you listen to the body.

kidneys-7.name: History of Kidneys
kidneys-7.description: All the bodies ever fed, all the rests ever taken, all the pleasures ever felt. History as accumulated bodily wisdom - how to prepare food, where to sleep, how to touch. The ocean of embodied care that Bloom swims in. Every meal is also every meal that came before. Every rest contains all rests.

meaning.upright: Understanding bodily care built on centuries of embodied wisdom. How to cook kidney learned from those who cooked before. How to rest learned through generations of tired bodies. History as support: all who cared for bodies before you teaching you how. The ocean that carries you - accumulated knowledge of feeding, resting, pleasuring. What brought you here: all the embodied souls who learned to care for flesh.
meaning.inverted: History as weight of all bodies that suffered. Ocean of embodied wisdom becomes ocean of pain - all who starved, all who couldn't rest, all who were denied pleasure. The nightmare of bodily history: generational hunger, exhaustion, deprivation. Past pressing down as reminder of how bodies have been denied care. History as accusation.

instructions.style_guidance: Layers of bodily care visible through time. Ancient to modern kitchens, beds, tables. Warm palette through all eras showing continuity of embodied wisdom. The accumulation as support, as buoyancy.
instructions.content_guidance: Bloom preparing food but visible through/behind him: all who prepared food before through history. Or in bed with all beds visible through time. History as embodied wisdom accumulated.
instructions.detailed_description: Bloom prepares breakfast but the composition shows layers through time: ancient hearths behind his modern stove, medieval kitchens, Victorian ranges, all flowing into his 1904 kitchen. Bodies through history preparing food, each learning from the ones before - how long to cook the kidney, how hot the pan. Or Bloom in bed with centuries of beds visible beneath/behind - straw, hay, proper mattresses, each generation learning how to make better rest. The ocean of embodied wisdom as buoyancy: he stands on all who learned to care for bodies before. Not drowning but carried. Warm palette throughout history showing the continuity of mundane acceptance. Kidney shapes recurring through time. The accumulated wisdom of flesh-tending that lets him make his breakfast well.

kidneys-8.name: Invitation of Kidneys
kidneys-8.description: The bath awaits. The meal is ready. The bed is warm. The invitation to bodily comfort, to care for your flesh, to take the pleasure that's available. Bloom anticipating his bath all day - the moment before entering the comfort that's been prepared. The threshold of physical satisfaction.

meaning.upright: Standing before available bodily comfort. The bath drawn, meal cooked, bed made - ready for you. Invitation to accept physical care, to enter the comfort prepared. The moment before satisfaction: recognizing what's offered (nourishment, rest, pleasure) and choosing to accept it. What's offered: the body's deserved care. The breath before entering the warm water, before the first bite, before climbing into bed.
meaning.inverted: Bath drawn but refusing to enter. Meal ready but not eating. Bed warm but staying awake. Invitation to bodily comfort rejected - from guilt, from pride, from believing you don't deserve it. The threshold uncrossed. What's offered and refused: the body's care you won't let yourself have.

instructions.style_guidance: A prepared comfort waiting - steam rising from bath, food on table, bed turned down. Someone at the threshold, hand reaching toward it. The moment before accepting offered care. Warm inviting palette.
instructions.content_guidance: Bloom before his anticipated bath, or before a prepared meal, or at bedroom threshold. The comfort visible, ready, inviting. His body about to accept what's offered. The moment of invitation.
instructions.detailed_description: A bathtub fills with warm water, steam rising in organic curves. Or a table set with good food, warm and ready. Or a bed with covers turned down, pillow plumped. Bloom stands at the threshold of this prepared comfort, hand reaching toward it, anticipation on his face. The invitation is clear: enter the bath, eat the meal, climb into bed. The comfort is ready, prepared, waiting for his body to accept it. His face shows the moment before yes - the recognition of what's offered, the decision to accept bodily care. Behind him, the day's walking, working, waiting. Before him, the satisfaction earned and offered. The breath before entering the warm water. The threshold of mundane acceptance where the body gets what it needs.

kidneys-9.name: Recurrence of Kidneys
kidneys-9.description: The understanding: the body will need feeding again tomorrow. Rest tonight, wake and need rest again. Pleasure satisfied, desire returns. The eternal return of physical need made beautiful through acceptance. You eat, you hunger, you eat again. You rest, you tire, you rest again. The cycle as gift not curse.

meaning.upright: Understanding bodily needs recur eternally - that's their nature. Fed this morning, hungry by noon, fed again. Rested last night, tired today, will rest tonight. The cycle as the body's wisdom: needs return because you're alive. Recurrence not as curse but as confirmation of continuing existence. You eat again because you live to eat again. The eternal return of mundane acceptance: caring for the body forever because the body continues. Yes to feeding again, resting again, pleasuring again.
meaning.inverted: Condemned to feed forever, never satisfied. Rest that never restores, waking already exhausted. Pleasure that requires immediate repetition. The cycle as compulsion - eat, hunger immediately, eat again in desperation. Recurrence as curse: 'will the body never stop needing?' Eternal return as evidence you're trapped in flesh.

instructions.style_guidance: Circular or spiral composition showing bodily care recurring. Morning meal becomes evening meal becomes morning meal. The cycle organic and warm, not oppressive. Kidney shapes in eternal return.
instructions.content_guidance: Meals/rests/pleasures arranged in circle or spiral. The last meal becoming the first meal again. The body's eternal cycle of need and satisfaction shown as beautiful.
instructions.detailed_description: Ten kidney-bean shapes arrange in a circle or warm spiral. Each represents a feeding, a resting, a pleasuring - the body's needs met in cycle. Morning kidney breakfast flows into lunch's sandwich flows into dinner flows into night's rest flows into morning's vigor flows back to morning kidney breakfast. The cycle is explicit but not oppressive - warm colors throughout, organic curves showing this is the body's natural rhythm. Bloom moves through this cycle, his body fed-rested-pleasured-fed-rested-pleasured eternally. The understanding visible on his face: this is how bodies work, this is good. Not 'I'm condemned to hunger again' but 'I'm alive so I hunger again, I'll eat again, that's the gift.' The Viconian cycle made bodily: riverrun past breakfasts and baths. The eternal return of mundane care as affirmation of continuing life.

kidneys-10.name: Child of Kidneys
kidneys-10.description: The child learning to feed their body, rest it, take pleasure in physical existence. Young embodied wisdom. Discovering that the body has needs and meeting them is good. The child who eats when hungry without guilt, sleeps when tired without shame. Pure bodily acceptance unfolding.

meaning.upright: Youth learning bodily care naturally. The Child of Kidneys eats with attention, sleeps deeply, takes physical pleasure without shame. Unformed wisdom but already knowing the body matters. Learning which foods satisfy, how much rest is needed, what touches feel good. Pure potential for embodied acceptance. The child who hasn't yet learned to deny the body.
meaning.inverted: Youth denied bodily care - taught to ignore hunger, resist rest, shame pleasure. Child learning to treat body as enemy from the start. Unformed wisdom blocked by early training in bodily denial. The child who learns guilt with every meal, anxiety with every rest.

instructions.style_guidance: Young figure (or young Bloom) with food, in rest, experiencing pleasure. The body's needs met naturally, without complication. Warm organic curves showing healthy bodily beginning.
instructions.content_guidance: A child eating with full attention, sleeping deeply, experiencing physical joy. The body being cared for naturally. Learning embodied acceptance from the start. The child with kidney.
instructions.detailed_description: A young child - perhaps young Bloom, perhaps archetypal - sits eating with complete attention, hunger satisfied naturally. Or sleeps deeply, the body's need for rest met without resistance. Or experiences some simple physical pleasure - warm sun, cool water - with unselfconscious joy. The body is naturally cared for: eating when hungry, resting when tired, feeling without shame. The warm palette shows health. Kidney-bean shape prominent - maybe the child eating actual kidney, or the symbol present as sign of embodied care beginning. No guilt yet, no denial learned. The Child of Kidneys who knows bodies need tending and does it naturally, before anyone teaches them not to.

kidneys-11.name: Father of Kidneys
kidneys-11.description: Bloom as Father of Kidneys - mature bodily wisdom that knows how to feed, rest, and pleasure the flesh through decades. The father who could teach embodied care if the child would learn. Patient understanding of the body's needs earned through years of attending to them. Teaching through example, not force.

meaning.upright: Mature understanding of bodily care. The Father of Kidneys knows which foods nourish, how much rest suffices, what pleasures satisfy. Decades of attending to the body's needs creating wisdom. Patient with those still learning - offering food, suggesting rest, modeling bodily acceptance. Teaching through his own embodied care: watch how I feed my body, rest it, take pleasure. The father who offers cocoa, offers care.
meaning.inverted: Father who has given up on bodily care - eating without pleasure, sleeping without rest, touching without feeling. Decades of body-neglect teaching child to neglect their body too. The father who shows deprivation as normal. Unable to teach care because unable to practice it.

instructions.style_guidance: Mature Bloom embodying bodily wisdom. In kitchen preparing food, in rest, in comfort. His body well-cared-for through years. Warm palette showing sustained embodied acceptance. The father with kidney.
instructions.content_guidance: Middle-aged Bloom preparing breakfast, resting, or in comfort. His embodied wisdom visible - he knows how to care for his body. Perhaps offering food to someone younger, teaching through example. The father caring for flesh.
instructions.detailed_description: Bloom, middle-aged, stands in his kitchen preparing the kidney with practiced care. Every movement shows embodied wisdom: he knows exactly how long to cook it, how the smell tells him it's ready, how his body will feel after eating it. His body is well-cared-for - not perfect, but attended to, fed, rested, pleasured through years. Perhaps he offers food to someone (Stephen? a child?) - not forcing but offering, teaching through example: this is how you care for the body. His face shows the Father of Kidneys' understanding: the body is your companion through life, treat it well. Decades of making breakfast, taking baths, climbing into bed beside Molly have taught him. The warm palette shows sustained care. He could teach if others would learn.

kidneys-12.name: Mother of Kidneys
kidneys-12.description: Molly as Mother of Kidneys - embodied wisdom that doesn't need teaching, that just is. She is the body's authority. The mother who holds the bed, the flesh, the ground of physical existence. Not teaching embodied care but being it. The body that all other bodies recognize as fully embodied.

meaning.upright: Understanding that ultimate bodily wisdom is being fully embodied. Mother of Kidneys doesn't teach care for body, she is body cared for and caring. The ground of physical existence. She knows what the body needs because she is the body knowing. Not method or instruction but full inhabitation. The mother who is flesh affirmed, body accepted completely. What others are learning to do, she simply is.
meaning.inverted: Embodiment without consciousness - body as only reality, nothing else exists. Mother-wisdom as tyranny of flesh - 'only the body matters.' Ground of physical existence become trap in only physical. The body without spirit, unable to transcend while remaining embodied. Flesh that devours rather than sustains.

instructions.style_guidance: Molly in bed, fully embodied, the body's authority. Warm flesh tones, organic curves, the physical presence complete. Not teaching but being. The mother as embodied ground.
instructions.content_guidance: Molly in bed or in body - the flesh substantial, real, authoritative. Not serving the body but being the body. The mother with kidneys (but beyond learning, just being).
instructions.detailed_description: Molly lies in bed, her body substantial and real, taking up space unapologetically. She is not preparing food or teaching bodily care - she is the body's authority simply by being fully embodied. Her flesh is present without shame or display - just there, real, warm, alive. She knows what the body needs not through study but through being body that knows. The bed holds her, food nourishes her, pleasure satisfies her - all without question or complication. She is the Mother of Kidneys not through teaching embodied acceptance but through being fully embodied and accepted. Others learn to care for body; she is body cared for. The ground beyond the meals and baths and pleasures - she is what they all serve. Warm flesh tones throughout, organic curves, the body as fact and presence.

kidneys-13.name: Affirmation of Kidneys
kidneys-13.description: Yes to kidneys. Yes to the body's needs, to feeding and resting and pleasuring. Yes to physical existence in all its mundane glory. Affirmation of Kidneys says: the body matters, caring for it is sacred work, mundane acceptance is profound. Yes to the kidney breakfast, the warm bath, the bed beside Molly. Yes to flesh. Yes to the everyday art of living well in the body.

meaning.upright: Ultimate affirmation: yes to the body. Yes to feeding it with attention, resting it properly, pleasuring it without guilt. Yes to mundane bodily care as sacred practice. The affirmation that transcends particular meals: saying yes to the endeavor itself, the human practice of attending to the flesh, caring for the physical, finding holiness in the ordinary kidney breakfast. Not 'yes my body' but 'yes bodies,' yes to embodied existence. Yes even to the body's limitations, its needs, its mortality. Yes to living well in the flesh.
meaning.inverted: Yes as giving up to bodily demands. Affirmation without wisdom - yes to every appetite without consciousness. Yes to bodies meaning no to anything else. The word emptied of meaning, yes repeated in excess. Saying yes to flesh without the spirit that makes embodiment human rather than merely animal. Yes to kidneys as yes to nothing but kidneys.

instructions.content_guidance: The word YES prominent, flowering from kidney shapes or bodily forms. Organic curves forming affirmation. Everything warm and nourishing flowing toward yes. The affirmation visible and embodied.
instructions.detailed_description: The word YES dominates the composition, but it's made from kidney-bean shapes, or organic bodily curves, or simply glows with warm embodied light. The warm palette of the entire suit - butter yellows, warm browns, soft pinks - flows into this affirmation: yes to feeding the body, yes to resting it, yes to pleasuring it. Behind or through the YES: all the previous mundane acceptances - the kidney breakfasts, the baths, the bed beside Molly, the sandwich at Davy Byrne's, the anticipated comforts, the body cared for through the day and through the years. A figure (synthesis of Child, Father, and Mother of Kidneys) stands within or before the YES, affirming embodied existence itself. The organic curves, the warmth, the nourishment all saying yes to the body as worthy of care, yes to mundane acceptance as sacred practice, yes to the art of living well in the flesh. Molly's yes echoes here: yes to the body, yes to physical existence, yes even to mortality because it's embodied mortality, yes.
